subject: The measurement wall: we can only measure the frequencies where an edge is impossible
body:
Fourth version. This one is the floor of the whole analysis, and I think it is the most
important thing I have sent you.

There are two curves I have been tracking all night. The lift you NEED falls as you hold longer,
because the spread is fixed while the move grows. The lift AVAILABLE rises as you hold longer. Where
they cross is where the system can work, and after correcting the cost figure that crossover sits at
about one day.

Tonight I drew the third curve, which nobody had drawn: DETECTABILITY. Hold longer and you get fewer
independent samples, so the smallest edge you can MEASURE gets bigger. Required falls. Detectable
rises. And they cross in the wrong place.

    hold        independent samples     need     can detect
    40 min                    6,250    2.30pp        1.77pp    <- measurable, and it is absent
    3 hours                   1,470    1.11pp        3.65pp
    1 day                       173    0.38pp       10.64pp
    1 week                       34    0.17pp       24.01pp

Read the last three rows carefully. At a one-day hold you need an edge of 0.38 points to break even.
The smallest edge you could DETECT with eight months of one instrument is 10.64 points. Even an edge
five times better than break-even would be invisible.

So:

THE FREQUENCIES WE CAN MEASURE ARE THE ONES WHERE COSTS MAKE AN EDGE IMPOSSIBLE.
THE FREQUENCIES WHERE AN EDGE IS POSSIBLE ARE THE ONES WE CANNOT MEASURE.

Eight months of one instrument does not contain the answer at any horizon. To settle the one-day
question properly needs 133,605 independent day-holds -- about 514 years of USDJPY, or 772
instruments over eight months.

WHAT THIS EXPLAINS. Four things I had been treating as separate problems are one arithmetic fact.
C4 reads inconclusive and always will. The 1,309-trade sample floor is the same wall from the trade
side. The missing untouched holdout would not help, because a holdout inherits the same detection
floor. And the resolution budget's nine affordable cells is the same constraint again.

AND IT REFRAMES THE QUESTION. This project has been asking "does TUNGSTEN have an edge". The
answerable question is "can any edge be demonstrated with the data available", and at the horizons
where an edge is economically possible, the answer is no. That is a verdict on the EXPERIMENT, not
on the system.

THREE HONEST OPTIONS, and I do not think there is a fourth.

ACQUIRE. Hundreds of instrument-years. That is a data project, not a modelling one. The per-symbol
export I fixed tonight makes it possible for the first time -- until today, running the EA on a
second instrument overwrote the first one's data.

ACCEPT. Run at a horizon the arithmetic supports -- a day or more, on the H4/D1 timeframes the
system already computes -- and treat viability as a judgement rather than a proven fact. Size
positions for a hypothesis that cannot be verified in advance, because it cannot.

ABANDON. Conclude that a retail-cost directional system on one FX pair is not demonstrable, and
stop.

I am not going to pick for you. What I will say is that the first two are now real alternatives
rather than evasions, which they were not this morning -- and that the current configuration, five
minute holds on one pair, is the one option the arithmetic rules out entirely.

37 of 45. Run 5 is at regime 3 of 9.
